dimensions.evidence: Executed x86-64 sizes: entry80, registry160, lease16, OwScope208 and each typed map32 bytes. Both private module pools occupy48 bytes (two instances), verified with nm rather than exposing a private client header.

Registry retains two opaque instances and up to four strong-reference obligations, with shared owner/context storage supplied separately. A stack OwScope holds up to three acquisition rollback entries in its eight-entry representation.

Generation tokens retain logical identity only; registry identity stays live/stable. Borrowed core callbacks outlive their module. Shared continuation retains actual OwShared dependencies and consumes the live lease before cleanup.

Complete operations are serialized. Read and IO owners may coincide and then acquire/release two references. Output/control/context aliasing otherwise excluded; typed map key/value correlations apply to direct typed calls.

Both private module factories use two actual static typed objects. Shared construction performs actual retains and conditional cleanup; no new dynamic allocation. Dead/count-overflow/full boundaries return without leaking the acquired prefix.

Contexts and registry cannot move while borrowed. A lease copies identity fields without duplicating ownership; only one valid close consumes the generation. Neither private representation is copied into a public byte buffer.

Close clears entry, closes module, releases IO then read. OwShared last-value/control destruction callbacks can perform external work and must satisfy the imported no-failure/no-reentry contract; elapsed destructor cost is not bounded by reference-count operations.

Actual separate O2 original code contains two indirect callback calls; GCC alternative uses one call site in a two-iteration loop, Clang unrolls to two call sites. Both invoke twice. Controller passes clock/sink subsets to separate leaves; erased context ownership remains a caller relation.
Non-atomic OwShared and registry are intentionally single-owner. No synchronized pointee access, cross-thread lease disposal or process authority follows from the generation checks.

Four acquisition cuts and independent underlying/wrapper exhaustion preserve output and existing entries. Failed clock output is staged; failed sink effects remain visible. Both implementations match75 independent service traces. Compiler-negative clients test private-field and cross-key/value access.

Actual separate clean builds and private-implementation-only rebuild/relink/run commands are recorded for GCC/Clang and both implementations. Same public header and client object are retained for incremental rebuild. Diagnostics constrain ordinary typed calls, not deliberately erased/cast inputs.
